brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four hex bases (piece:0,0 full; piece:1,0 full; piece:0,1 full; piece:-1,0 half-w) with capOpenFaces end caps (12 solid caps) and lockJoints bolts (3 jointBolts). check_build: ok, meshClash clear, no issues.

notch:0#-1,1 with stem hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf (notch drawer frame) fills the empty position between bases (-1,0) and (0,1). No separate drawer part was listed by find_sockets; the drawer is the notch drawer frame.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 (mount variant) sits at the junction where bases (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0) meet, level 0.
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on the same spike junction. The solid spike refused platforms (TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED), so I swapped it for the mount variant, which accepted it.

finish.summary: Built a small desk unit: three full hex bases and one half base in a compact footprint, a notch drawer frame between the west half base and the south base, a mount-type spike at the three-base corner carrying a small platform, plus house-rule caps and joint bolts. The configurator reports no issues and a clear mesh check. Material, load and strength are not verified.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
